## A linter?

<br>

Find code that is not optimal, likely wrong, hard to read, etc.

. . .

<br>

So far in R: **`lintr`**

- 117 rules (formatting + linting), e.g. `any(is.na(x))` -> `anyNA(x)` 
- reports lints, does not fix them
- can be slow
- requires an R setup

##

<br><br>

{{< fa arrow-right >}} &nbsp; **`Jarl`**

- ~ 40 rules (linting only)
- fast (uses Air infrastructure)
- automatic fixes when possible
- single binary to run

<br>

Full docs: [jarl.etiennebacher.com](https://jarl.etiennebacher.com/)

# 1. How to use

## 1. How to use

<br>

Three options:

- in terminal:

```sh
# Run linter on current directory
jarl check .

# Run linter and apply automatic fixes
jarl check . --fix
```

. . .

- with extensions (Positron, Zed, VS Code, Neovim, Helix): code highlighting and code-actions

. . .

- in CI: Github actions workflow [setup-jarl](https://github.com/etiennebacher/setup-jarl)

## 1. How to use

<img src="./screenshot_ci.png" width="700" height="200">

:::{#yaml-ci}
```yaml
# Workflow derived from https://github.com/posit-dev/setup-air/tree/main/examples

on:
  push:
    branches: main
  pull_request:

name: Lint

permissions: read-all

jobs:
  jarl-check:
    name: jarl-check
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
      - uses: etiennebacher/setup-jarl@v0.1.0
```
:::

# 2. How to configure

## 2. How to configure

<br>

**With CLI arguments** (temporary)
<br>
<br>

```sh
# Use the rules "any_is_na" and "any_duplicated" only
jarl check . --select any_is_na,any_duplicated

# Use all default rules + testthat rules except "expect_named"
jarl check . --extend-select TESTTHAT --ignore expect_named

# Get a more concise version of rule violations
jarl check . --output-format concise

# All commands
jarl check --help
```

## 2. How to configure
<br>

**With `jarl.toml`** (permanent)
<br>
<br>

Most CLI args have an equivalent in `jarl.toml`:
<br>

```{.toml filename="jarl.toml"}
[lint]
extend-select = ["TESTTHAT"]
ignore = ["implicit_assignment", "numeric_leading_zero"]
assignment = "="
```

. . .

<br>

Some arguments are identical to `air.toml`, e.g. `default-exclude`.

<br>

CLI arguments always override `jarl.toml` arguments.


# 3. How to extend

## 3. How to extend

<br>

Requirements to add rules:

- need knowledge of Rust

- need basic knowledge of `tree-sitter` Abstract Syntax Tree (AST)

- no plugin mechanism, changes must be integrated in Jarl directly.

. . .

<br>

:::{.callout-note #note-rust appearance="simple"}
I'm not a Rust expert, other code improvements are also welcome!
:::

. . .

<br>

Main limitations (for now):

1. No code flow analysis

2. No access to the R environment

## 3. How to extend

<br>

1. No code flow analysis

<br>

Jarl can only do pattern detection.

. . .

For example, detecting unreachable code is not possible:

```r
foo <- function(x) {
    if (x > 10) {
        return("hi")
    } else {
        return("bye")
    }
    x + 1 # unreachable
}
```

## 3. How to extend

<br>

2. No access to the R environment

<br>

* Don't know from which package the function comes.

. . .

* Sometimes okay, e.g. `testthat`:

    - quite distinct prefix (`expect_`)
    - partially overlapping namespace with `tinytest` but we don't use both at the same time

&nbsp; &nbsp; &nbsp; &nbsp; &nbsp; &nbsp; {{< fa arrow-right >}} &nbsp; can let the user opt in the rule group `TESTTHAT`

. . .

* Some packages have more generic function names and could be more problematic.
